claim: Without high-throughput mode, each partition of an SQS FIFO queue is limited to 300 transactions per second for each API action (SendMessage, ReceiveMessage and DeleteMessage).
question: SQS FIFO throughput without high-throughput mode (transactions per second per API action)?

qualifiers.scope: per partition of a FIFO queue, per API action; non-high throughput mode
qualifiers.condition: High throughput mode surpasses this default limit.

evidence.quote: Each partition in a FIFO queue is limited to 300 transactions per second, per API action (SendMessage, ReceiveMessage, and DeleteMessage). This limit applies specifically to non-high throughput mode.

note: The queue-types page says 300 API calls per second per API method for the whole queue; the quotas page says per partition. The quotas page is used as current truth.

claim: With batching, an SQS FIFO queue that is not in high-throughput mode supports up to 3,000 messages per second for each API action; that is 300 API calls, each with a batch of 10 messages.
question: SQS FIFO throughput without high-throughput mode (messages per second with batching of 10)?

qualifiers.scope: per API action (SendMessage, ReceiveMessage, DeleteMessage); non-high throughput FIFO queue
qualifiers.condition: Each API call carries a batch of 10 messages.

evidence.quote: If you use batching, non-high throughput FIFO queues support up to 3,000 messages per second, per API action (SendMessage, ReceiveMessage, and DeleteMessage). The 3,000 messages per second represent 300 API calls, each with a batch of 10 messages.

claim: In high-throughput mode, an SQS FIFO queue supports up to 70,000 transactions per second (non-batched API calls) in US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon) and Europe (Ireland).
question: SQS FIFO high-throughput mode: the Region-dependent maximum transactions per second?

qualifiers.scope: per queue; non-batched API calls; US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Europe (Ireland); high throughput mode
qualifiers.condition: Other Regions have lower limits; a higher limit can be requested in Service Quotas.

evidence.quote: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), and Europe (Ireland): Up to 70,000 transactions per second (TPS).

note: The queue-types page still says high throughput mode scales up to 30,000 transactions per second; the quotas page is used as current truth.

claim: In high-throughput mode, the default throughput of an SQS FIFO queue in AWS Regions that are not named in the Region list is 2,400 transactions per second (non-batched API calls).
question: SQS FIFO high-throughput mode: the Region-dependent maximum transactions per second (all other Regions)?

values.spoken: two thousand four hundred transactions per second

qualifiers.scope: per queue; non-batched API calls; all AWS Regions not listed separately; high throughput mode

evidence.quote: All other AWS Regions: Default throughput of 2,400 TPS.

claim: In high-throughput mode with batched API calls, an SQS FIFO queue supports up to 700,000 messages per second in US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon) and Europe (Ireland), which is 10 times the non-batch limit of 70,000 TPS.
question: SQS FIFO high-throughput mode: what batching adds in the highest-limit Regions?

values.spoken: seven hundred thousand messages per second

qualifiers.scope: per queue; batched API calls; US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Europe (Ireland); high throughput mode
qualifiers.condition: Each batched call carries up to 10 messages.

evidence.quote: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), and Europe (Ireland): Up to 700,000 messages per second (10x the non-batch limit of 70,000 TPS).

qualifiers.scope: per standard queue, per API action

evidence.quote: Standard queues support a very high, nearly unlimited number of API calls per second, per action (SendMessage, ReceiveMessage, or DeleteMessage).

claim: For most standard queues, there can be a maximum of approximately 120,000 in-flight messages (received by a consumer but not yet deleted), depending on queue traffic and message backlog.
question: SQS in-flight message limit for standard queues?

values.spoken: about one hundred twenty thousand in-flight messages

qualifiers.condition: Depends on queue traffic and message backlog; a quota increase can be requested.

evidence.quote: For most standard queues (depending on queue traffic and message backlog), there can be a maximum of approximately 120,000 in flight messages (received from a queue by a consumer, but not yet deleted from the queue).

claim: When a standard queue reaches the in-flight message quota, short polling returns the OverLimit error message, and long polling returns no error messages.
question: What happens at the SQS in-flight limit with short versus long polling?

qualifiers.scope: standard queues at the in-flight message quota

evidence.quote: If you reach this quota while using short polling, Amazon SQS returns the OverLimit error message. If you use long polling, Amazon SQS returns no error messages.

claim: FIFO queues support a maximum of 120,000 in-flight messages (received by a consumer but not yet deleted); when the limit is reached, Amazon SQS does not return an error, but processing may be impacted.
question: SQS in-flight message limit for FIFO queues, and what happens at the limit?

values.spoken: one hundred twenty thousand in-flight messages

qualifiers.condition: An increase beyond this limit can be requested through AWS Support.

evidence.quote: FIFO queues support a maximum of 120,000 in-flight messages (messages received by a consumer but not yet deleted). If this limit is reached, Amazon SQS does not return an error, but processing may be impacted.

note: The FIFO limit was 20,000 in older material (history row dated 2024-11-21; the decisions+changes lens records the change).

claim: An SQS queue name can have up to 80 characters; alphanumeric characters, hyphens and underscores are accepted.
question: SQS queue name rules: maximum length?

qualifiers.condition: Accepted characters are alphanumeric characters, hyphens and underscores. Queue names are case-sensitive.

evidence.quote: A queue name can have up to 80 characters. The following characters are accepted: alphanumeric characters, hyphens (-), and underscores (_). Queue names are case-sensitive (for example, Test-queue and test-queue are different queues).

claim: The name of an SQS FIFO queue must end with the .fifo suffix, and the suffix counts towards the 80-character queue name quota.
question: SQS queue name rules: FIFO queue name suffix .fifo?

values.display: counts towards the 80-character queue name quota

evidence.quote: The name of a FIFO queue must end with the .fifo suffix. The suffix counts towards the 80-character queue name quota.

claim: There is no quota to the number of message groups within an SQS FIFO queue.

batching can substantially reduce your costs

claim: In an SQS FIFO queue, messages with the same deduplication ID sent within a 5 minute deduplication interval are treated as duplicates, and only one copy is delivered.
question: SQS FIFO deduplication interval (a duplicate with the same deduplication ID is not delivered within how long)?

qualifiers.scope: per FIFO queue, per message deduplication ID

evidence.quote: If multiple messages with the same deduplication ID are sent within a 5 minute deduplication interval, they are treated as duplicates, and only one copy is delivered.

claim: With content-based deduplication, Amazon SQS uses a SHA-256 hash of the message body, but not of the message attributes, to generate the message deduplication ID.
question: How does SQS FIFO content-based deduplication build the deduplication ID?

values.display: but not the attributes of the message

qualifiers.scope: SQS FIFO queues with content-based deduplication enabled

evidence.quote: Enable content-based deduplication. This instructs Amazon SQS to use a SHA-256 hash to generate the message deduplication ID using the body of the message—but not the attributes of the message.

values.display: the number of times a consumer can receive a message from a source queue
before it is moved to a dead-letter queue

evidence.quote: The maxReceiveCount is the number of times a consumer can receive a message from a source queue before it is moved to a dead-letter queue.
